text: Only three notes allowed.
Play just two notes, and make them count.
Use only the root and the fifth.
Stay on one single note for the whole first half, then break free.
Only notes from the pentatonic scale.
Every phrase must end on the root.
No note may repeat twice in a row.
Avoid the root completely. Circle around it without landing.
Play only the chord tones of whatever chord you imagine underneath.
Pick a favourite note and come back to it at the start of every phrase.
Only play on the off-beats.
Play only on beat one of each bar.
Quarter notes only. Steady as a heartbeat.
Use only short, detached notes.
Leave a full bar of silence after every phrase.
Every phrase starts on the "and" of beat two.
Play in triplets against the straight beat.
Phrase in groups of five, ignoring the bar line.
Repeat one rhythm for the entire jam and only change the notes.
Call and answer yourself: two short notes, then rest, then two more.
Start at a whisper and build over 8 bars.
Play as quietly as you possibly can.
Alternate loud and soft every bar.
Start loud and fade to nothing over 8 bars.
Play the whole thing at medium-soft, like a late-night conversation.
Crescendo on every held note, then cut off clean.
Build to one huge moment, then drop to silence.
Accent every first beat and keep the rest gentle.
Stay in the lowest octave you can play.
Stay in the highest octave you can play.
Start low and climb a little higher every four bars.
Never move more than two steps at a time.
Only leap: every interval must be a third or bigger.
Stay inside a span of five notes.
Alternate between your lowest and highest comfortable range every phrase.
Use only your weaker hand for the picking, strumming or fingering you normally lead with.
No open strings.
Only open strings, plus the occasional octave harmonic if you dare.
Only one hand on the keys. Pick whichever you like.
Play with your left hand only.
Slide into every note.
Use only hammer-ons and pull-offs: no picking after the first note of a phrase.
Play every note with a slap or a pop, as percussive as you can.
Use rim clicks and cross-sticks only. No cymbals.
Play the whole thing with brushes or fingers, no sticks.
Keep the hi-hat or ride going with your foot and hand while the other hand tells a story.
Breathe only at the end of four-bar phrases.
Use only long tones, each held for at least two beats.
Sing or hum every note before you play it.
Use vibrato on every note that lasts longer than a beat.
Play every note staccato, light and bouncy.
Play every note legato, as smooth as you can.
Play it like a lullaby.
Play like you are walking on tiptoe past a sleeping dragon.
Play as if the sun is just coming up.
Tell a story with no words: a beginning, a problem, and a happy ending.
Play like a robot learning to dance.
Imitate a thunderstorm rolling in, then passing.
Play the angriest happy music you can.
Play like you are underwater.
Pretend the next note is your very last. Make it mean something.
Copy the sound of a bird: short chirps and long calls.
Play a different character each bar: a villain, a hero, a ghost, a clown.
Play like you are a little bit bored and a little bit amazing.
Make every phrase a question that never quite gets answered.
Play it sweet, then play it sour, then play it sweet again.
